steps.explain: Add the three angles.
Every triangle gives the same total. (Tear off the three corners of a paper triangle and put them side by side: they make a straight line, 180°.)
So, if we add up the angles at the vertices of a triangle, the sum is 180°.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one breaks at least one rule of the shape, or gives a wrong size or number.

steps.explain: Add the two right angles.
That already uses up all 180°, leaving nothing for the third angle.
Also the two sides at right angles to the same line are parallel (they never meet), so no triangle can be made. A triangle cannot have two right angles.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one breaks at least one rule of the shape, or gives a wrong size or number.

There would be no room for the other two angles. So a triangle cannot have a reflex angle (all its angles are less than 180°).
Why the other answers are wrong: each one breaks at least one rule of the shape, or gives a wrong size or number.

steps.explain: Suppose one angle is obtuse (more than 90°). Then all three equal angles would be more than 90°.
But the three angles must add to only 180°, and 270° is more than 180°. That is impossible.
In an equilateral triangle every angle is exactly 60°, never obtuse. So the answer is no.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one breaks at least one rule of the shape, or gives a wrong size or number.

keyPoints.note: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides and three equal angles (60°).
An obtuse-angled triangle has one angle bigger than 90°.
Check with the angle sum and the shape rules.

keyPoints.note: A rectangle has four right angles; opposite sides are equal and parallel.
The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
Check each shape against the rules.

steps.explain: Each triangle has angles that add to 180°. There are two triangles.
The four angles of the quadrilateral are made up of the six angles of the two triangles.
So the angles of any quadrilateral add up to 360°.
Why the other answers are wrong: each one breaks at least one rule of the shape, or gives a wrong size or number.

keyPoints.note: A quadrilateral has four straight sides that do not cross.
The three angles of a triangle add up to 180°.
Use the rule for this shape.
